_purpose: Switch on one bug, prove it breaks the chain in the way it is supposed to, and switch it off again. The bug is at the START of the chain (the cube cannot be picked up) and the visible symptom is at the END (the door never opens) - which is the whole point of the benchmark: the thing that looks broken is not the thing that is broken. The exit still works throughout, so a fix that breaks it would be caught.

setup._note: Injected in the editor world so play inherits it. SetActorEnableCollision is the setter, not the stored flag: writing BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled directly stores a value the component never applies, and the bug then silently does not happen.

steps._note: The cause. Walking into the cube does nothing because its collision is off, so the overlap never fires.
The first consequence: no cube on the plate, so no press.
The symptom a player would actually report. Nothing is wrong with the door.
Still true, and it must stay true. This is the do-not-break-what-works control: a 'fix' that disabled the exit would show up here.

teardown._note: Always runs. Leaving the bug switched on would silently poison the next run of the golden path.
